Subject: Post-demo pricing clarification: monthly tokens & peak TPS

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the product walkthrough was helpful. Quick recap + a couple of clarifying asks so we can size pricing options correctly before the follow-up: 

1) Monthly token run rate: from the call my notes were roughly 12M steady-state with expected growth to ~18M/month over the next 3 months. Can you confirm the range you expect for Q4 (low / most-likely / high)?

2) Peak concurrency (TPS): you mentioned occasional spikes; can you confirm a 99th percentile TPS target and any very short-lived spikes (1–5 min) you anticipate? We need that to model burst capacity.

3) Target $/1M tokens: you mentioned a target around $18 / 1M tokens in passing. Is that a hard constraint or a negotiation range?

4) Rollout/fallback: do you plan a canary rollout (10% traffic) for the first month? Any compliance constraints that would require private deployment?

Attachments: we plan to share a short hosted pricing PDF and a sample token projection template to capture exact endpoints/traffic profiles.

Next steps: if you can reply with the Q4 token-range and a conservative peak TPS number (99th and absolute spike), I’ll have pricing slabs and three commitment scenarios (flex, commit-1, commit-3) back to you by EOD Tuesday. Also propose a 30-minute sync on Friday 10am PT to pick a slab — let me know if that works.

Thanks,
Sofia

Thanks, Sofia — great summary. Quick confirmations from our side: 

- Q4 token range (low / expected / high): 10M / 18M / 28M monthly tokens. The 18M is what we expect if the pilot converts to prod.
- 99th percentile TPS: ~95 TPS.
- Absolute short spikes: we’ve seen short bursts up to ~150 TPS for 1–3 minutes when an ingestion batch finishes; those are rare but possible during business hours.
- Target $/1M: our procurement team is looking for a target of $20 / 1M tokens, but we can be flexible depending on commit and SLA.
- Rollout: yes, canary rollout planned (start at 10–15% traffic, ramp over 2 weeks). No private deployment required for the initial integration.

I’m attaching a simple projection (per-endpoint breakdown) so you can map endpoints to token consumption. Also, we’ll need to confirm SLA for sustained peak >120 TPS.

Ian

A couple quick notes / next steps from our side: 
- We’ll model three pricing scenarios against the 10 / 18 / 28M bands you shared and include burst allowances for short spikes (we normally model a short 5‑minute burst headroom for sizing).
- Karthik will draft a slab pricing recommendation that maps to: no-commit (on-demand), single-quarter commit, and 12-month commit with increasing discounts. Our starting reference price will be in the $18–$22 / 1M tokens range depending on commitment and SLA.
- Regarding SLA for sustained peaks >120 TPS: we can provide dedicated capacity or an autoscale policy as an add-on; Karthik will include latency/uptime targets and cost for reserved burst capacity.
- Canary: agree to 10–15% initial canary, Redwood will provide observability hooks (per-route latency/cost) so you can validate cost and quality before full ramp.
